checks: Read all nine submission pages and the exact government bill identified on the committee cover.
Checked the complete quota schedule in proposed BImSchG section 37a(4), physical page 9. Its last step is 59 percent from calendar year 2040.
Visually inspected the full original physical page 7, including both the disputed first paragraph and later separate 2040 subquota description.
adversarial_assessment: The natural endpoint reading is a five-year slip: the author introduces an increase up to 59 percent in 2045, whereas the schedule first reaches it in 2040. However, the text does not expressly say first or only in 2045, and an open-ended 59 percent requirement does also apply in 2045. The surrounding paragraph criticizes the level and feedstock pressure, rather than contrasting 2040 with 2045 or relying on an additional five-year transition. This benign reading is affirmative, not merely missing evidence.
reason_for_conservative_recommendation: A narrow date-description finding is defensible editorially, but it depends on construing an implied endpoint. To satisfy the instruction not to treat an uncertain reading as a proved error, I recommend keeping it as an unresolved wording lead unless another passage establishes the intended first-attainment date.
limits: No finding that 59 percent is wrong, that the quota is absent in 2045, or that the feedstock or fraud policy concerns are disproved. No motive inference.
quote_note: No new verbatim quotation recorded; the original source quotation allowance is preserved.
